value.title: pij Rust port — base PRD (requirements register)
value.source: Started 2026-08-28 per Jordan ('start a PRD spine, much like flowspace3'); fs3 docs/plans/prd/base-prd.dd.json is the pattern; CI rows pinched from fs3 workflows per Jordan (native agents, no Intel Mac).
value.register_discipline: Lynx's earned rules (fs3 register in practice, 2026-08-28): (1) one row per PROVABLE CAPABILITY, never per feature-noun — rows that can carry a receipt get closed, vague ones accrete annotations forever. (2) completed_evidence is prose unless a consumer RE-EXECUTES it — at least one reviewer/gate must re-run the evidence (AC receipts + probe-flip done bars are the working form); reviewers are told to disbelieve the field. (3) SPLIT a row the moment two different seats need to own the halves (ownership is the boundary); ANNOTATE when evidence changes but the owner doesn't. (4) A row's wording never claims more than its evidence — when they diverge, fix the CODE to match the promise, never the promise to match the code.

value.title: Rust implementation
value.requirement: pij ships as a single Rust binary (pij-rs during coexistence): CLI and daemon are two composition roots in one executable; Command::Daemon short-circuits into the daemon so CLI and daemon version together.

value.title: Full verb parity with the TS CLI
value.requirement: Every production pij verb reaches parity, proven by byte-goldens for computed payloads against the TS binary on the same store — not by eyeball.
value.note: golden mechanism lands in plan 108 (Q4 ruling); verb surface = wave 3

value.title: SQLite store with self-migration
value.requirement: All state in SQLite via sqlx: embedded checksummed migrations, daemon self-migrates at boot, stale-schema refused loudly both skew directions (newer binary migrates forward; older binary refuses).

value.title: Queue-first daemon
value.requirement: Handlers do one cheap DB statement; all real work is enqueued with dedupe (partial-unique over live jobs) and per-entity serial claims.

value.title: Ports + shipped fakes, offline-first
value.requirement: Seven frozen port traits (Registry, Spine, Queue, Transport, TmuxPort, HarnessPort, LivenessPort) with deterministic fakes in testkit; the whole system runs offline end-to-end with fakes as default config.

value.title: Mechanical architecture drift gate
value.requirement: Crate-dependency allowlist with per-row rationale, enforced by a test, negative-proven; every new edge is a reviewed one-row diff.

value.title: CLI-daemon over local-only HTTP
value.requirement: Envelope {ok,command,v,data,meta}, per-boot 0600 bearer key written before bind, NDJSON event stream with Hello line and Unknown variant — portable across macOS/Linux/Windows with no socket platform splits. AUTH (fs3 #43 pattern, source-verified auth.rs 2026-08-28): one 256-bit key minted per daemon boot, 64 lowercase hex, written 0600-before-bytes via same-dir tempfile + atomic rename, published BEFORE the listener binds (race designed out); Authorization: Bearer on EVERY route, /health included (whole-router middleware, no exemption list); raw HTTP client private behind the authenticated wrapper so the type system refuses bypass; 401 envelope carries key_file detail + next_action naming the exact path and the self-heal; key path+format are FROZEN CONTRACT (CLI, doctor, tests, restart-verify all consume it). Config-dir trap from fs3's one real incident: if the daemon serves the default port under a non-default config root, refuse or mirror the key to the ambient location — the key file's LOCATION is part of the credential.
value.note: fs3 req-0017 pattern auth per lynx source-grounded answer + crates/daemon/src/auth.rs (read whole; tests encode the contract)

value.title: Honest delivery receipts
value.requirement: send/inbox with queued|delivered|held receipts that mean what they say; pre-bind messages queue instead of vanishing; every route logs message id + outcome.

value.title: Liveness by (pid, proc_start)
value.requirement: No liveness verdict from a bare pid; recycled pids detected structurally; revive distinguishes registry-missing from native-artifact-missing and resolves artifacts at the correct per-harness path.

value.title: Supervision that consults declared state
value.requirement: Watchdog eligibility respects semanticState (waiting/hold/blocked/question are not stalls); thresholds configurable; every computed signal has a consumer.

value.title: Cross-platform CI on native runners
value.requirement: CI and release build on native agents: ubuntu-latest (x86_64), ubuntu-24.04-arm (aarch64), macos-14 (aarch64-apple-darwin), windows-latest (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc). NO Intel Mac (x86_64-apple-darwin excluded, Jordan 2026-08-28, matching fs3's 2026-08-26 ruling). Pinched from fs3 release.yml: pinned toolchain, --locked builds, per-target smoke-run of the built binary, fast test tier on each target.

value.title: Attribution hooks the write sink
value.requirement: Agent attribution is recorded where bytes land, not at the tool surface — EVAL-batch writes and any future modality leave a trace.
value.note: lynx finding: turtle's ~60 EVAL-written files invisible to git-ai

value.title: Daemon lifecycle better than fs3's
value.requirement: Single-instance guard day 1; a real supervise/restart/upgrade story is designed (not a tmux pane + memory file); C6 restart affordances built in.

value.title: Coexistence and cutover behind parity
value.requirement: TS and Rust run side-by-side against the same store during migration; the TS CLI retires only after a soak behind the parity harness; cutover is its own plan. Cutover asymmetry (Jordan 2026-08-28): claude/copilot/codex seats survive the daemon swap live (outside-bound, subprocess CLI only — no restart); pi/OMP seats carry the in-process extension and change over version-gated behind a logged compat shim, never flag-day.

value.title: Reusable eventing system
value.requirement: One in-process pub/sub event primitive serves every near-real-time consumer — inbound message routing, file-watch notices, bg command completion, watchdog nudges, seat state changes — typed Event enum with an Unknown variant, durable tail via the spine (replayable), live tail via the NDJSON stream. New event kinds are additive, never a version bump; no consumer polls.
value.note: Jordan 2026-08-28: 'reusable eventing, not just message routing — file watches, backgrounds, etc.'

value.title: pi and OMP extension updated and proven in both hosts
value.requirement: The in-process pij extension speaks the pij-rs wire (envelope v + Hello detection, one build spans the cutover window) and is PROVEN live in both hosts: the same extension build boots in plain pi AND in OMP, registers with bind evidence, receives a pushed turn, and replies — one committed transcript per host.
value.note: Jordan 2026-08-28. Owning unit u-extension (wave 3); cutover-design phase 5 consumes it.

value.title: Cross-machine federation: a daemon per machine, LAN-only, key-trust, @machine addressing
value.requirement: pij works across machines on the local LAN: every machine runs its own daemon with its own local database; daemons route seat traffic to each other over the existing HTTP surface. Trust is the bearer key (LAN-only deployment; no TLS of our own). Seat addresses gain a machine part — <seat>@<machine-alias>, alias from daemon config defaulting to hostname; an unqualified name always means local, so single-machine usage is unchanged. v1 scope: messaging, registry visibility, and spine events across machines; remote spawn works the normal way once a daemon runs there (a prime spawns as per now via the remote daemon) — daemon bootstrap on a new machine is manual, no remote provisioning.
value.note: Jordan 2026-08-30, iterated one-question-at-a-time: federation over hub (ruled), LAN+key trust (ruled), seat@machine shape (ruled), manual first-daemon + normal prime spawn thereafter (ruled). Lands in wave 3 with u-daemon-http/u-cli: bind_addr, key exchange, and address parsing must account for this now, not retrofit.

value.title: Daemon auto-rebuild-and-restart on merge to main (adopt lynx mechanism)
value.requirement: pij adopts flowspace3 daemon build-and-restart so the live daemon restarts automatically when work merges to main: build, health-check, restart sequenced without dropping in-flight deliveries, with a guard against restarting mid-delivery. Applies to the TS daemon immediately (tsx off source, no hot-reload, restarts are manual and forgettable today) and carries into the Rust daemon post-cutover.
value.note: Jordan 2026-08-30: lynx has a way to build and restart their daemon that we should adopt, then restart auto when merging to main as we work. Mechanism details requested from pij-instant-lynx (pointers pending); port not wrap.
